rv.q: We Are Your Robots skips elegantly back and forth between profound curiosity and endearing hilarity.
But taken as a whole, the show, which is directed by Leigh Silverman, feels stifled by slightly monotonous whimsy.
Ethan Lipton's We Are Your Robots dives headfirst into the Artificial Intelligence conversation with easily the most entertaining theatrical foray into the subject yet.
The ruefully philosophical We Are Your Robots, on the other hand, is a chamber piece that’s as much live concept album or illustrated lecture as stage musical...
We Are Your Robots will please Lipton's fans and may add a few new ones, too.
If you go into We Are Your Robots expecting to enjoy 80 percent of it, you'll be just fine.

cn.t: Critics find this robot musical charming but uneven, with strong performances and an inventive premise that doesn't fully deliver on its conceptual promise.

vr.q: The comedic tone of the piece, the design elements, and the music itself all had a charmingly retro feel that was fitting to the themes, and the music was definitely the highlight for me.
